title: Cartier Santos: the watch made for a man who flew

slides.title: The watch made for a man who *flew.*
slides.body: In 1900, a real gentleman kept his watch in his pocket. One aviator changed that.

image.credit: Alberto Santos-Dumont by Nadar · Public domain

slides.title: Wristwatches were for *women*
slides.body: Men carried **pocket watches on chains.** Watches worn on the wrist were mostly seen as ladies' jewelry. Then a Brazilian started flying over Paris.

slides.title: The dandy of the *skies*
slides.body: Rich, elegant and fearless, Santos-Dumont flew his own airships over Paris and became a celebrity. **He was also a close friend of Louis Cartier.**

slides.title: Try reading a pocket watch while *flying*
slides.body: As the story goes, Santos-Dumont told Cartier that **checking a pocket watch in flight was nearly impossible** with both hands on the controls.

slides.title: Louis Cartier's *answer*
slides.body: According to Cartier, the answer was a square watch **strapped to the wrist**, with a bold bezel and visible screws. Easy to read, elegant enough for the salons.

slides.title: Into the *record books*
slides.body: Santos-Dumont flies his 14-bis **220 meters in about 21 seconds**: Europe's first officially certified powered flight, and the first world aviation record.

image.credit: The 14-bis, 12 November 1906 · period newspaper illustration · Public domain

slides.title: Everyone *wants one*
slides.body: In 1911 **Cartier puts the Santos on sale.** A watch on a man's wrist starts to look modern, not feminine. The First World War will finish the job.

slides.title: Over a century later, the screws are *still there.*
slides.next: The Quartz Crisis: the watch that almost killed Swiss watchmaking

caption:
Before 1904, a wristwatch on a gentleman was seen as women's jewelry. ✈️

Brazilian aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont needed to check the time without letting go of the controls. His friend Louis Cartier designed a square watch with a leather strap, and helped make the men's wristwatch a normal thing.

Fun fact for time travelers: his record-breaking flight happened on November 12. ⚡

Sources: Cartier; FAI; Quill & Pad; Wikipedia.
